basis: Strongylid infection umbrella ([MeSH](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/mesh/68017206)); intestinal hookworms dominate human cases; extraintestinal sites depend on species.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: most human strongylid infections are intestinal, especially hookworm; rare extraintestinal species do not determine umbrella labels.

basis: Intestinal lymphangiectasia and ID define syndrome; microtia 8/8 and camptodactyly 5/8; blepharophimosis 6/9 omitted at cap. Hearing impairment alone occurs in only 2/9.

decisions.cardiovascular: none: lymphatic dysplasia alone does not establish heart or blood-vessel damage within this axis; pericardial lymphangiectasia has no frequency.
decisions.neurologic: primary: intellectual disability is a defining Hennekam feature, present in 7/9 patients.
decisions.ocular: none: blepharophimosis in 6/9 qualifies structurally but is omitted at the cap in favor of universal microtia and functionally limiting contractures.

basis: Neuromuscular-junction disorder; myopathy occurs in 30-79%, with documented muscle-fiber atrophy. Ocular motor, swallowing and respiratory weakness alone do not establish eye, gut or lung injury.

decisions.ocular: none: ptosis and ophthalmoparesis reflect neuromuscular-junction dysfunction; direct ocular tissue damage is not established.
decisions.musculoskeletal: involved: myopathy occurs in 30-79%; muscle-fiber atrophy documents structural muscle involvement beyond fatigability.

basis: Portal venous hypertension; hepatic nodular regenerative hyperplasia 2/5 (40%); splenomegaly 9/9 with thrombocytopenia 8/9 (~89%). Esophageal varices are vascular.

decisions.hepatic: involved: nodular regenerative hyperplasia affects 2/5 (40%); hepatic parenchymal disease is not required to define noncirrhotic portal hypertension.

basis: Neurodevelopmental disease; VSD 60%, hypospadias 50% (urethral malformation), skeletal defects 30-40%; hypodontia 30% omitted at the four-axis cap.

decisions.renal: involved: hypospadias affects 5/10 (50%) and directly malforms the urethra, which belongs to the renal axis.
decisions.gastrointestinal: none: hypodontia in 3/10 (30%) qualifies but is omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent urethral and skeletal malformations and cardiac defects.

basis: Deafness, psychomotor impairment and cleft palate are explicitly defining features; PDA/pulmonary arterial hypertension occur in 30-79%. Cleft palate qualifies despite its 5-29% annotation.

decisions.gastrointestinal: primary: cleft palate is explicitly part of the disease definition; defining oral malformations qualify without meeting the involvement frequency threshold.

basis: Transient ammonia metabolism disturbance; asymptomatic forms lack demonstrated brain injury, and direct neurologic damage in >=30% across the full spectrum is unestablished.

decisions.neurologic: none: asymptomatic forms lack deficits ([study](https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/3511207/)); neurologic injury in >=30% across the whole concept is unestablished.

basis: Hydrocephalus, gut atresias, renal defects and tracheoesophageal fistula occur in 80-99%; severe airway defects retained. Ocular (80-99%), skeletal/cardiac (30-79%) omitted at cap.

decisions.pulmonary: involved: tracheoesophageal fistula directly malforms the trachea in 80-99%; retained for frequency and severity under the four-axis cap.
decisions.ocular: none: corneal/optic nerve anomalies occur in 80-99% but are omitted at the cap in favor of severe brain, gut, renal and airway defects.
decisions.musculoskeletal: none: vertebral and radial malformations occur in 30-79%; omitted at the cap in favor of more frequent, severe organ defects.

basis: Limb absence and bilateral lung agenesis define this subtype; cleft palate directly affects the mouth in 6/7 (~86%). Pulmonary vein hypoplasia 2/7 (~29%) is below threshold.

decisions.pulmonary: primary: bilateral lung agenesis defines this subtype (5/7); [OMIM summary](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/gtr/conditions/C4747923/).

basis: Cobalamin remethylation disorder with characteristic inherited megaloblastic anemia; neurologic/developmental impairment is common (roughly >=30%); published series are small.

decisions.haematologic: primary: inherited megaloblastic anemia is a core phenotype ([JBC](https://www.sciencedirect.com/science/article/pii/S0021925820770201)), consistent with its hereditary-anemia ancestry.
